top_signals.title: Wall Street Week | Debt & Consequences, Defying Fiscal Gravity, Hollywood Gets Democratized
top_signals.summary: This week, Chrystia Freeland talks with the former finance ministers of the Netherlands and Germany about what it takes to bring spending under control. And, are US deficits now a bigger driver of interest rates than inflation? Plus, as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh makes his debut at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, we revisit the story of the wealthiest place in America. Later, the rise of YouTube filmmakers is democratizing discovery, while also flooding the market with more content than audiences can watch. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Yen weakens past ¥160 per dollar, eroding intervention gains
top_signals.summary: Traders now are carefully watching yen levels for signs of when authorities might move to protect the currency.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.
